summary.text: A 52-year-old male presented with a lump in the right iliac fossa and weakness for 3 months. He was non-hypertensive and non-diabetic. Examination showed severe pallor and a well circumscribed, non-tender 5.5 × 4.5 cm lump with restricted mobility. He had received a few units of blood transfusion for severe anaemia before presenting.

Haemoglobin was 5.4 gm/dL with hypoproteinaemia. CT showed a circumferential neoplastic lesion in the caecum with colo-colic intussusception and a heterogeneously enhancing round left adrenal lesion measuring 5.5 × 5.3 cm, suggestive of AML. Colonoscopic biopsy showed a well-differentiated carcinoma of the caecum. Plasma normetanephrine was elevated at 218.00 ng/L, while plasma-free metanephrine and the other endocrine tests were within normal limits.

A multidisciplinary tumour board decided on left adrenalectomy with right hemicolectomy, which were performed with an uneventful post-operative period. Histopathology showed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with free margins, nine of 31 lymph nodes positive, and lympho-vascular and perineural invasion (pT3N2b). The adrenal lesion was reported as adrenal lipoma with haemorrhagic infarction and fat necrosis, although other text calls it AML.

He received adjuvant oral capecitabine 1,500 mg twice daily from day 1 to day 14 with oxaliplatin 200 mg on day 1, repeated every 21 days for 8 cycles. He was doing well and under regular follow-up for the last 1 year.
